headline: Tokyo Electric Power and other Japanese utilities are tightening their electricity rules for data centers to stop operators from reserving more grid power than they end up using.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: only the opening paragraph of the paywalled article could be read, so the rules themselves are unverified.
importance_line: It affects companies that reserve power for data centers in Japan and the utilities that must plan around those reservations, but what the new rules require and when they start are not yet known.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Tokyo Electric Power Co. Holdings is among the Japanese utilities tightening its electricity rules for data centers to stop "capacity squatting", meaning reserving more grid power than ends up being used.
notes: Paywall: only the opening paragraph, standfirst and caption were readable; no other outlet found. Summary is kept to what that paragraph says.
